exposure: Umbilical cord milking 10 times for 10-15 seconds
outcome: Bilirubin level at 72 hours of life
cohort: 162 full-term pregnant women undergoing elective cesarean section at a single center between November 2021 and June 2022
finding: Umbilical cord milking was more effective than delayed cord clamping for enhancing hemoglobin and hematocrit levels in newborns delivered by cesarean section, with no significant difference in bilirubin levels at 72 hours of life.
mod_finding: Umbilical cord milking was more effective than delayed cord clamping for enhancing hemoglobin and hematocrit levels in newborns delivered by cesarean section, with no significant difference in bilirubin levels at 72 hours of life.
